definitions: Points are pairs of integers, with origin o = (0,0). For every natural number p (including zero), a jump from u to v means that each coordinate of v − u lies inclusively between −p and p; staying still is allowed, and for p = 0 it is the only jump. The box of natural radius N is the set of points whose two coordinates lie in [−N,N], so radius zero gives {o}. A journey of power p is a finite nonempty list beginning at o whose consecutive entries are jumps of power p; the one-entry list [o] is a journey, repetitions are allowed, and indices for which either consecutive entry is absent impose no constraint. A Devil strategy is any total function from finite point lists to an optional point, with no point meaning a pass; an Angel strategy is any total function from a finite point list and a finite list of optional points to a point. These functions are defined even on empty, inconsistent, or otherwise illegal histories. A state consists of these two lists, without invariants; its current point is the last point in its first list, or o if that list is empty. Starting with point list [o] and empty optional-point list, each round first appends the Devil's response to the existing point list to the optional-point list, then appends the Angel's response to the old point list and this extended optional-point list to the point list. This recursion defines play for every natural number of rounds, even after an illegal move. The Angel survives with power p against a Devil precisely when, in every round starting at round zero, its new point is a jump of power p from its preceding point and is unequal to every point the Devil has selected up through that round. Repeated selections, passes, and selection of the occupied point are otherwise allowed; selecting the occupied point alone does not invalidate a round if the Angel leaves it legally. AngelWins(p) means that a single Angel strategy survives against every Devil strategy. A Devil is nice at power p precisely when on every journey of power p, every point it selects is different from o and is not a jump of power p from any entry before the last entry of that journey; passing imposes no restriction, non-journey inputs impose no restriction, and on [o] only selection of o is forbidden. Escaping means that for every natural N there is a natural round n at which the current point lies outside the box of radius N; this does not require eventually remaining outside that box. NiceAngelWins(p) means that one Angel strategy both survives and escapes against every nice Devil. NiceCanConfine(p,N) means that one nice Devil has the following property for every Angel strategy and every natural n: if each of the first n rounds has a jump of power p and a new point unequal to every point selected by the Devil up through that round, the current point after n rounds belongs to the box of radius N. This condition includes finite legal prefixes that have no infinite legal continuation; for n = 0 its premise is vacuous and its conclusion is the true assertion that o belongs to the box.
reduction: For every positive natural number p, assume that there does not exist a total Angel strategy that survives against every total Devil strategy, where points are integer pairs, the Angel starts at (0,0), a Devil strategy maps each finite list of Angel positions to either a point or a pass, and an Angel strategy maps that position list together with the list of Devil responses to its next point. In each round the Devil responds first, and the Angel then responds after seeing that response; survival means that in every round each coordinate changes by at most p in absolute value and the new point is unequal to all points selected by the Devil so far, including in that round. Then there exist a positive natural number N and one Devil strategy D such that (i) for every nonempty finite position list starting at (0,0) with all consecutive coordinate changes at most p in absolute value, any point selected by D is different from (0,0) and has a coordinate difference of absolute value greater than p from each position occurring before the last entry, and (ii) for every total Angel strategy A and every natural number n, if all first n rounds of the recursively defined play of A against D satisfy the stated movement and avoidance conditions, then both coordinates of its position after n rounds lie in [−N,N]. Passes and repeated selections are permitted; D has no restrictions on position lists failing the stated journey condition, while on the singleton origin list it is only forbidden to select the origin. Staying still is a permitted jump. The strategies and play are total, including after failures; the confinement conclusion concerns every finite safe prefix, whether or not it extends to infinite survival. At n = 0 its premise is empty and its conclusion concerns the origin. The assumption rules out a single universally surviving Angel strategy; it does not itself posit a single universally defeating Devil strategy.
nice_win: There exists a total function A taking a finite list of integer-pair positions and a finite list of optional integer-pair Devil responses to an integer-pair position, such that the following holds for every total Devil function D from finite position lists to optional points satisfying this restriction: on every nonempty position list starting at o = (0,0) in which each coordinate changes by at most 2 in absolute value between consecutive entries, any point selected by D is different from o and, for each entry before the last entry, differs from that entry by more than 2 in absolute value in at least one coordinate. Starting from position list [o] and no Devil responses, recursively in each round append D's response to the position history to the response list, then append A's response to the old position history and extended response list to the position history. For every natural round n, the newly appended position differs from the preceding position by at most 2 in each coordinate and is unequal to every point selected by D in the first n + 1 rounds. Moreover, for every natural N, including zero, there exists a natural round n such that at least one coordinate of the position after n rounds has absolute value greater than N. Thus the same A satisfies both assertions for every D obeying the restriction. Passes and repeated selections are allowed, staying still is a permitted jump, D is unrestricted on histories failing the stated condition, and on the singleton origin history its only forbidden point is the origin. The functions remain defined on empty or inconsistent inputs, and the recursion continues even after failure. The escape assertion requires an exit at some time for each box, without an eventual-stay-out condition; n = 0 is an allowed quantified time but cannot witness an exit because its position is o.
main_goal: There exists one total Angel function A mapping a finite list of integer-pair positions and a finite list of optional integer-pair Devil responses to an integer-pair position such that, for every total Devil function D mapping finite position lists to optional points, the following infinite sequence of rounds survives: begin at o = (0,0), with position list [o] and no Devil responses; in each round first append D's response to the current position list to the response list, and then append A's response to the old position list and the extended response list to the position list. For every natural round n, including zero, each coordinate of the new position differs from the preceding position by at most 2 in absolute value, and the new position is unequal to every point selected by D through that round. A Devil response may be a pass or any integer-pair point, including a repeated selection or the Angel's occupied point, and no niceness restriction is imposed. Staying still is permitted as a move only when the landing point has not been selected by the Devil. Strategies are total even on empty or inconsistent histories, and play is recursively defined even after an invalid move, though the stated A guarantees that no such invalid move occurs against any D. No additional assertion that the Angel's positions leave every bounded box appears in this declaration.
